long_biography.plain_text:
Kuwaiti merchant Abdulaziz Alshaya learned English in Bombay after his father sent him there for schooling. He subsequently worked in the family's Indian trading business. When new rules required a local partner in 1952, he left the shop with an Indian associate and returned to Kuwait, where expanding infrastructure offered new commercial opportunities.

His public work included helping establish a committee to collect charitable donations in 1954. He later chaired the committee and was a cofounder of the Kuwait Red Crescent Society. He also helped found the local Al Shamiya cooperative society.
